note: The small network's profile total on the current patch, against r2026-11-10-1-profile's 6.296 ms at 1080p on the same instrument. The developer reports that the `port-profile-small` entry was requested earlier and has been added to the policy, but with a different env from the one the plan item proposed - so read the run's OWN output before its numbers. `tools/port_profile.sh`'s second line of output is `model:  <dir>`, and that single line decides everything below it: if it prints `/opt/neuralscreen/model` rather than the small directory, the entry is running the large network and the numbers are a repeat of r2026-11-10-1-profile dressed as a result, which is the silent-null failure this project has hit before. The script honours exactly two env names - `NEURALSCREEN_MODEL_DIR` and `NEURALSCREEN_PORT_BIN` - so an entry setting anything else changes nothing and says nothing. If the entry is not in the policy at all, the runner refuses the request and pushes the refusal, which is also an answer. On the numbers: this is a re-measure, not a re-run of a dead idea. The only port sample is r2026-10-30-aq, 26.5 ms against the large network's 24.6, and that is an October run on an older patch, before the port derived its stage table from the manifest; the public reads of the 310.9.16 model (the 2026-11-09 survey: 8.8 -> 5.4 ms at 4K on this card, 36-40% lower GPU time elsewhere) call it the faster one, and it has never been checked against the current schedule. Gate it like any measurement - if gpu_before reads BUSY, or idle_waited_s is not 0.0, say so and do not compare. If it wins, the fps half needs the same trick on a `minimal`-shaped entry (`NS_WORKER_CMD` naming `serve --model /opt/neuralscreen/model-small`), which is a second line for the developer.
